subtitle: Two cities with room to get lost

body: Midtown Madness 3 is Digital Illusions CE's Xbox driving game, first released in North America on 17 June 2003. Paris and Washington, D.C. become open spaces for races, jobs and aimless driving. The cities are condensed interpretations rather than exact reproductions, arranged to make familiar streets and landmarks part of a playable road network. Choosing a vehicle and setting out can be an activity of its own. The game keeps the series' interest in urban freedom while moving its console debut to a new developer and a new machine.

Checkpoint races ask the player to reach a set of markers, making knowledge of the streets useful alongside speed. Blitz events add a time limit, while Cruise allows traffic, weather and time of day to be adjusted for a less directed journey. The Work Undercover campaign gives driving another context through jobs such as deliveries, taxi work and emergency services. A familiar road can therefore become part of several different problems. Learning a shortcut or recognising an approaching junction makes the city more useful every time the player returns.

Split-screen play brings another driver into the same room, while Xbox Live originally opened the streets to online groups. Some modes revolve around chasing or touching another vehicle; others ask players to carry gold to a hideout or keep possession of a target. These rules turn the open map into a shared playground rather than only a racing circuit. Olof Gustafsson composed the music. The original Xbox Live service closed in 2010, but the game's mixture of free driving and structured events remains a distinctive part of the console's racing library.
